title: Here He Passed on Foot Through These Streets
text:
Here he passed on foot through these streets,

without employment or post and without a peso.

Only poets, whores, and drunks

knew his verses.


He was never abroad.

He was in prison.

Now he is dead.

He has no monument...


But

remember him when you have concrete bridges,

great turbines, tractors, silver granaries,

good governments.


Because in his poems he purified the language of his people,

in which one day trade agreements will be written,

the Constitution, love letters,

and decrees.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the poet's poverty and imprisonment against the future public language he helped purify.

title: Yesterday I Saw You
text:
Yesterday I saw you

in the street,

Myriam and


I saw you so beautiful,

Myriam, that


(how can I explain

how beautiful I saw you!)


Not even you, Myriam,

can see yourself

so beautiful

or imagine

that you can be

so beautiful to me

and I saw you so beautiful

that it seems that


No woman

is more beautiful than you


No man in love

sees any woman

so beautiful,

Myriam,

as I see you


And not even you yourself,

Myriam,

are perhaps

so beautiful


Why

can so much beauty

not be real!


As beautiful as I saw you

yesterday in the street


Or as today it seems to me,

Myriam

that I saw you
editorial_note: The translation keeps the breathless repetitions and the slightly dangling 'Myriam and' from the source.

title: Epigram XX
text:
One wakes to cannon fire

in the morning

full of airplanes

it would seem to be

the revolution

but it is the birthday

of the tyrant.

Ileana

the Andromeda galaxy,

700,000 light-years

which can be

seen with the naked eye

on a clear night

is closer than you

other solitary eyes are

looking at me from Andromeda,

in their night

I do not see you.

Ileana, distance is time,

and time flies.

At 200 million

miles per hour

the universe

is expanding

toward nothingness

and you are far

from me as if

millions of years away.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the collision of tyrant's birthday spectacle with the Andromeda-distance love poem.

title: There Is a Place Beside
text:
There is a place beside

the Tiscapa lagoon


—a boat beneath

a quelite tree—


that you know

(the one to whom I write


these verses will know

that they are for her)


And you remember

that bench and

that quelite;


The moon reflected

in the Tiscapa lagoon,


The lights of the palace

of the dictator


the frogs singing

down in the lagoon


That quelite

tree is still there


The same lights

are still shining;


In the Tiscapa lagoon

the moon is reflected;


But that bench

tonight will be empty


Or with another couple

who are not us.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Tiscapa's repeated lights and moon while the remembered bench loses the lovers.

title: I Saw Many Years Ago
text:
I saw many years ago from a bus in Virginia or Alabama

a rosy girl, in blue pants

up on a ladder, picking apples

(the mother calling from inside)

and another girl, the sister, blue pants

painting the house porch white

-And they looked toward the bus that was passing and speeding up.

Time has passed like the Greyhound bus

but there remained, despite the years, the fresh

paint on the porch

the dripping brush

the hand on the apple, the glances

years ago, one morning, Virginia or Alabama

the state is forgotten.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the fleeting Greyhound image and the exact uncertainty of Virginia or Alabama.
